bnqZzhIv544.speaker_note: speaks of our London community, Western University, his upbringing in Syria and his Sunday tafsir after Maghrib
bnqZzhIv544.title: My Maxims, Part 6
bnqZzhIv544.one_line: Eight months into Gaza, he urges the community to back student encampments, support those who act without demanding full agreement, and carry its weight.
bnqZzhIv544.summary: Although billed as the sixth talk in his maxims series, he sets the maxims aside and speaks about Gaza eight months into the bombardment. Every generation has a blind spot, he argues, and this is ours, so being able to see truth as truth is a blessing that brings responsibility. He points to an unprecedented shift in public opinion, especially among young people who no longer heed their parents' advice to keep their heads down, and to the campus encampments. Causes are won when public opinion moves first, and narratives change in academia, so those tied to Western University should keep up the pressure and the community must physically, financially and morally back students who are risking their futures. Recalling his second maxim, he insists you do not need to agree with someone completely to stand with them, and that Muslims who act are too often left to burn alone. Drawing on the Quran's picture of the hypocrite as a freeloader who takes the perks without the buy-in, he says every Muslim, aged 10 or 90, must find a role, and that Jumuah exists to deliver a message that demands action. In the second khutbah he calls this rare global Muslim unity a wave from Allah that must be turned into organized work before the nafs lets it fade.

outline.heading: Opening
Gaza as this generation's blind spot
outline.gist: Eight months of bombardment and over 30,000 dead, mostly women and children, while the world debates its legitimacy. Every era has a blind spot; being able to see right as right is a blessing to be grateful for.

outline.heading: An unprecedented shift in public opinion
outline.gist: Muslims must be a voice for the voiceless. With the International Court of Justice ordering a ceasefire in Rafah, he has never seen opinion shift so sharply, especially among the young.

outline.heading: Causes are won when public opinion moves first
outline.gist: Keeping the momentum is a responsibility before Allah. Before the world wars, enough awareness had to build before anything changed politically; political change may still be far off, but public opinion is there.

outline.heading: The young no longer walk beside the wall
outline.gist: Fifteen years ago parents would have stopped the encampments. He was raised in Syria to keep his head down and stay out of politics; today's students are not listening to that fear, and advice given out of fear can be taken with a grain of salt.

outline.heading: Encampments succeed when the community stands behind them
outline.gist: The successful encampments in the US, Canada and Europe had people bringing food, wisdom and physical presence. London's students are risking degrees and careers, and we owe it to them to show up.

outline.heading: Keep pressing Western
outline.gist: Beyond showing up, those affiliated with the university should keep up the pressure. Almost every household here is tied to it, and academic institutions carry weight in the world.

outline.heading: Narratives change in academia, not from the minbar
outline.gist: One well-published PhD thesis moves politics more than a lifetime of khutbahs, so academics and people of wealth and status should push the issue and protect the students.

outline.heading: Those who act are left to burn
outline.gist: Muslims who stick their necks out often lose everything while the community looks away, and the youth learn never to speak up.

outline.heading: Maxim 2 again: support without full agreement
outline.gist: You will never agree with anyone 100 percent. Zoom out to the broad strokes and stand with your brothers and sisters even when their methods are not yours.

outline.heading: Withdrawing over a refused request is shameful
outline.gist: Staying home because your requested change did not happen means everyone must dance to please you. Ask whether we stand for justice and the oppressed; if so, the details can wait.

outline.heading: Mistakes are part of the process: the companions
outline.gist: The companions made many mistakes and lost battles, but agreement on why they acted kept them together; without that mentality Islam would not have come this far.

outline.heading: Gaza has quieted our disagreements
outline.gist: Over eight months people have come to see what they share; the disagreements that glared last September are less visible because everyone is focused on a bigger picture.

outline.heading: The double standard
outline.gist: Supremacist rhetoric from a country everyone backs is played down, though a Muslim saying the same with the target changed would be arrested. Ending it requires communities to unite behind those taking action.

outline.heading: Not everyone can march, but everyone carries weight
outline.gist: If you cannot go to the encampment, support it another way. This applies to everything in your deen and ummah: carry your weight.

outline.heading: The hypocrite is a freeloader
outline.gist: From his Sunday tafsir: the Quran's munafiq takes the perks of being Muslim without the buy-in, giving no time, wealth or effort.

outline.heading: The Prophet's count and the missing 600
outline.gist: Knowing he had about 1,500 able to bear arms, the Prophet called and 900 came. The gap between the count and the output is the freeloaders, who want only to pray and leave.

outline.heading: Jumuah is not about attendance
outline.gist: At university in Syria students called themselves slaves of the attendance mark. Jumuah is obligatory because its message must be heard and acted on, so each person can find a role.

outline.heading: Find your role: on the wagon or under it
outline.gist: Whether 10 or 90, everyone has a role and will be asked about it. Either you carry the ummah with everyone else or it carries you.

outline.heading: Interlude
Gaza has united Muslims as Syria did not
outline.gist: Muslims failed to unite over many clear injustices, including Syria's destruction and seven million displaced, but have come together over Gaza. Allah has brought hearts together.

outline.heading: Turn unity into work
outline.gist: The momentum must become commitment, organizing, advocacy and education for the next generation. This is not feeding off suffering but using what has happened as fuel.

outline.heading: Plan the next steps for the students
outline.gist: Use the unity to bring Islam back to the front despite racial and cultural differences, support the students and talk seriously about how to apply more pressure.

outline.heading: Courage is rising; do not be petty
outline.gist: People now say on social media what once cost them their accounts, because not everyone can be cancelled. He disagrees with much in the community but refuses to be an obstacle.

outline.heading: A historic wave from Allah
outline.gist: Keep it moving and criticize later. Muslims have been weak for some 300 years; unlike 1948, technology now lets Muslims across the globe hear one another, and only giving up can stop it.

outline.heading: The nafs that wants things quiet
outline.gist: The part of you that wants this to die down so you can return to trips and comfort is the nafs. Ignore it and let the strength Allah put in your spirit rise.

outline.heading: Outro

28:24.ar: فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَآ أَنزَلۡتَ إِلَيَّ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ فَقِيرࣱ‏
28:24.en: So he watered (their flock) for them. Then he turned aside into the shade, and said: My Lord! I am needy of whatever good Thou sendest down for me

28:25.ar: فَجَآءَتۡهُ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا تَمۡشِي عَلَى ٱسۡتِحۡيَآءࣲ قَالَتۡ إِنَّ أَبِي يَدۡعُوكَ لِيَجۡزِيَكَ أَجۡرَ مَا سَقَيۡتَ لَنَاۚ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُۥ وَقَصَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡقَصَصَ قَالَ لَا تَخَفۡۖ نَجَوۡتَ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
28:25.en: Then there came unto him one of the two women, walking shyly. She said: Lo! my father biddeth thee, that he may reward thee with a payment for that thou didst water (the flock) for us. Then, when he came unto him and told him the (whole) story, he said: Fear not! Thou hast escaped from the wrongdoing folk

28:26.ar: قَالَتۡ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱسۡتَـٔۡجِرۡهُۖ إِنَّ خَيۡرَ مَنِ ٱسۡتَـٔۡجَرۡتَ ٱلۡقَوِيُّ ٱلۡأَمِينُ
28:26.en: One of the two women said: O my father! Hire him! For the best (man) that thou canst hire in the strong, the trustworthy

28:27.ar: قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أُنكِحَكَ إِحۡدَى ٱبۡنَتَيَّ هَٰتَيۡنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأۡجُرَنِي ثَمَٰنِيَ حِجَجࣲۖ فَإِنۡ أَتۡمَمۡتَ عَشۡرࣰ ا فَمِنۡ عِندِكَۖ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أَشُقَّ عَلَيۡكَۚ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
28:27.en: He said: Lo! I fain would marry thee to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that thou hirest thyself to me for (the term of) eight pilgrimages. Then if thou completest ten it will be of thine own accord, for I would not make it hard for thee. Allah willing, thou wilt find me of the righteous

28:28.ar: قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَكَۖ أَيَّمَا ٱلۡأَجَلَيۡنِ قَضَيۡتُ فَلَا عُدۡوَٰنَ عَلَيَّۖ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلࣱ‏
28:28.en: He said: That (is settled) between thee and me. Whichever of the two terms I fulfil, there will be no injustice to me, and Allah is Surety over what we say

28:23.ar: وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدۡيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيۡهِ أُمَّةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسۡقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمۡرَأَتَيۡنِ تَذُودَانِۖ قَالَ مَا خَطۡبُكُمَاۖ قَالَتَا لَا نَسۡقِي حَتَّىٰ يُصۡدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُۖ وَأَبُونَا شَيۡخࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
28:23.en: And when he came unto the water of Midian he found there a whole tribe of men, watering. And he found apart from them two women keeping back (their flocks). He said: What aileth you? The two said: We cannot give (our flocks) to drink till the shepherds return from the water; and our father is a very old man

53:28.ar: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍۖ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّۖ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغۡنِي مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
53:28.en: And they have no knowledge thereof. They follow but a guess, and lo! a guess can never take the place of the truth

33:32.ar: يَٰنِسَآءَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ لَسۡتُنَّ كَأَحَدࣲ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِنِ ٱتَّقَيۡتُنَّۚ فَلَا تَخۡضَعۡنَ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ فَيَطۡمَعَ ٱلَّذِي فِي قَلۡبِهِۦ مَرَضࣱ وَقُلۡنَ قَوۡلࣰ ا مَّعۡرُوفࣰ ا
33:32.en: O ye wives of the Prophet! Ye are not like any other women. If ye keep your duty (to Allah), then be not soft of speech, lest he in whose heart is a disease aspire (to you), but utter customary speech

19:42.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ لِمَ تَعۡبُدُ مَا لَا يَسۡمَعُ وَلَا يُبۡصِرُ وَلَا يُغۡنِي عَنكَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
19:42.en: When he said unto his father: O my father! Why worshippest thou that which heareth not nor seeth, nor can in aught avail thee

38:23.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِي لَهُۥ تِسۡعࣱ وَتِسۡعُونَ نَعۡجَةࣰ وَلِيَ نَعۡجَةࣱ وَٰحِدَةࣱ فَقَالَ أَكۡفِلۡنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِي فِي ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:23.en: Lo! this my brother hath ninety and nine ewes while I had one ewe; and he said: Entrust it to me, and he conquered me in speech

37:102.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡيَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّيٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُۖ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
37:102.en: And when (his son) was old enough to walk with him, (Abraham) said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Allah willing, thou shalt find me of the steadfast

TdK3nOakTtg.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat al-Qasas, Musa in Madyan and the Marriage Offer (28:24-28)
TdK3nOakTtg.one_line: Musa in Madyan: when suspicion is a duty, respectful speech between the sexes, haya' as life, and making marriage easy.
TdK3nOakTtg.summary: He repeats that judging people is only conjecture; catching someone in one uncharacteristic moment tells you nothing. Best is not to assume at all, and if you must, assume well, with one exception: those responsible for others, a father vetting a suitor or someone guarding shared money, are obliged to be cautious. The Prophet held the people of faith to more, refusing Fatimah a servant and leaving the Ansar out of the spoils of Hunayn while entrusting them to their faith. Musa's exchange with the two women shows respectful, modest conversation between men and women is permitted; what is forbidden is suggestive speech and dress, and total segregation is a desert custom that leaves men untrained. The woman who walks with shyness opens a long discussion of haya': it comes from the word for life, it is responsiveness to what is around you, and it gives rise to courage and generosity. Her father hears only Musa's story yet trusts what his daughters saw, and the daughter names the ideal employee: strong and trustworthy. The father seeks a husband for his daughter, makes work the dowry and refuses to burden him, because making the halal hard pushes young people toward the haram. A wise father looks for character, and a husband must be patient with his wife.

outline.heading: Recap: scenes found only in al-Qasas
outline.gist: Musa's time in Madyan with his future wife and her father appears only here, because the surah is about relationships with people.

outline.heading: Judging is only conjecture
outline.gist: Whatever you know of someone's story, judging it is assumption, and assumption is no substitute for truth; every scene so far would mislead an onlooker.

outline.heading: Caught in an uncharacteristic moment
outline.gist: We often see people at a moment that does not reflect who they are, as anyone seeing Musa's blow would call him a tyrant.

outline.heading: Best not to assume at all
outline.gist: If you must, think well of people; and who has finished purifying himself enough to have time to assess others?

outline.heading: When suspicion is a duty
outline.gist: Responsibility requires caution: vetting a suitor, a business partner, or anyone handling public interests; it is not personal and not naive.

outline.heading: The educator's responsibility
outline.gist: Only when guiding and teaching someone may he look critically at them, to help them.

outline.heading: Fatimah's request for a servant
outline.gist: With hands roughened from grinding, she asked for help, and he gave her remembrance at bedtime instead.

outline.heading: Hunayn: Abu Sufyan told to carry it alone
outline.gist: Given vast spoils, Abu Sufyan asked for help carrying them; the Prophet's reply stayed with him for life.

outline.heading: The Ansar's grievance
outline.gist: After years of sacrifice the Ansar saw the spoils go to new converts; their leader admitted he shared his people's feeling.

outline.heading: Entrusted to their faith
outline.gist: He gave worldly scraps to the weak in faith and left the Ansar to their faith; they wept and said they were content with the Messenger.

outline.heading: Holding the people of faith to more
outline.gist: He prayed for the Ansar and their descendants; a believer does not measure himself by what others receive.

outline.heading: Musa spoke to two strange women
outline.gist: If answering a stranger were forbidden, neither he nor they could have spoken; the question is modesty and knowing one's limits.

outline.heading: The limits: dress and soft speech
outline.gist: What is forbidden is dressing to attract and speaking in a submissive, suggestive way.

outline.heading: Women who taught the men
outline.gist: Without Aisha and Umm Salamah teaching men, much of the Prophet's life would be lost to us.

outline.heading: Qawl ma'ruf: speech you would not be ashamed of
outline.gist: Proper speech is what you would say before her father or yours; ma'ruf is a social standard that the law gives weight to as custom.

outline.heading: Custom differs by place
outline.gist: Greeting a neighbour's wife is normal in one village and an outrage in the next town; teach children how to speak properly with the other sex.

outline.heading: The Prophet turned the young man's face
outline.gist: When a young companion stared at a woman asking a question during Hajj, the Prophet gently turned his face away: teaching manners, not banning interaction.

outline.heading: Total segregation is a desert custom
outline.gist: Khadijah was a trader who dealt with people; societies with no training produce men who harass women in the street.

outline.heading: Running from interaction brings no good
outline.gist: Avoiding all contact to spare ourselves trouble fails; recap of the women at the well and Musa's prayer.

outline.heading: She came walking with shyness
outline.gist: One of the two, his future wife, returns; the verse highlights her haya'.

outline.heading: Haya': the character of Islam, never excessive
outline.gist: Every religion has a character and Islam's is haya'; excess in other virtues harms, but more haya' is always better; it comes from the word for life.

outline.heading: Life is responsiveness
outline.gist: The living respond to what is around them; the tactless guest who overstays lacks it; Uthman's haya' coexisted with strong leadership.

outline.heading: Haya' in gaze, dress and public space
outline.gist: It governs gaze, tongue and dress, and the litterer in the park lacks it; awareness of others gives rise to courage and generosity.

outline.heading: Her shyness was dignity
outline.gist: Not coyness or flirtation; her composed respect is what caught Musa's attention.

outline.heading: Walk ahead of me
outline.gist: Out of modesty she guided him from behind with directions; whether the old man was Shu'ayb is debated, and the majority view is acceptable.

outline.heading: He told him the story: the father knew only that
outline.gist: The father knew Musa only through his own account, so he relied on what his daughters had witnessed, and reassured him he was beyond Pharaoh's reach.

outline.heading: Recitation: the offer and the agreement
outline.gist: He recites the daughter's advice, the marriage offer and Musa's acceptance.

outline.heading: Ya abati: tender address to a parent
outline.gist: The added ta is an Arab endearment for a father, also seen in Ibrahim's speech; she suggested hiring him since shepherding was hard on women.

outline.heading: The best to hire: strong and trustworthy
outline.gist: Strength to defend the flock and honesty to guard it, mirroring judgement and knowledge; a weak shepherd loses to a strong one, as in Dawud's case of the ewes.

outline.heading: Seek a husband for your daughter
outline.gist: The father looked further than hiring; a parent should seek a good husband for his daughter as he would a wife for his son.

outline.heading: Work as the dowry
outline.gist: Scholars differ on hire within a marriage contract; the Prophet married a woman to a man for teaching her Quran; 'hijaj' is an Arabic word, fitting Shu'ayb as one of four Arab prophets.

outline.heading: I do not want to burden you
outline.gist: Burdening the seeker of halal turns him toward haram, and then the right kind of suitor stops coming.

outline.heading: Marriage is easy in the shariah
outline.gist: A contract with a guardian, witnesses and consent makes it lawful and a cause for celebration with drums and song.

outline.heading: Make the halal easier than the haram
outline.gist: Inflated demands leave young people unmarried at thirty; if we make halal hard and then blame them for haram, the blame is ours.

outline.heading: Choosing a barefoot, hungry man
outline.gist: The father asked how Musa spoke and acted and chose him for character, unlike our weddings costing hundreds of thousands.

outline.heading: You will find me among the righteous
outline.gist: The father promises fair treatment, echoing Isma'il's words to Ibrahim; he proposes with dignity.

outline.heading: What a wise father looks for
outline.gist: Manhood means patience with a wife: if you dislike one trait in her you are pleased with another, not reacting like a child.

outline.heading: Abu Yazid al-Bistami and his wife
outline.gist: Turned away from a gathering of worshippers who could not match his patience with his wife, he went back to her; a lesson, not a literal model.

outline.heading: Musa accepts: whichever term I fulfil
outline.gist: Musa accepts and leaves the eight or ten years between them, with Allah as witness.

themes.label: Not judging others by their story
themes.note: Assumption is no substitute for truth; think well or not at all, except where responsibility requires caution.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Fatimah's request and the Ansar at Hunayn show the Prophet held the people of faith to more than worldly reward.

themes.label: Gender relations, chastity and modesty
themes.note: Respectful speech between the sexes is permitted; suggestive speech and dress are not, and total segregation leaves men untrained.

themes.label: Character and manners (akhlaq)
themes.note: Haya' is Islam's character, rooted in the word for life; it is responsiveness and the source of other virtues.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Seek a husband for your daughter, judge suitors by character, do not burden them, and be patient with your spouse.

themes.label: Work ethic, productivity and excellence (itqan)

x0QPizQR4XM.title: Between June 6th and Rafah, Part 1
x0QPizQR4XM.one_line: Between Gaza's nine months and June 6's third anniversary: the same hatred and indifference behind both, and how Muslims, especially youth, must change the narrative.
x0QPizQR4XM.summary: With Gaza nearing nine months and the third anniversary of the June 6 attack in London approaching, he asks Muslims to step back and learn rather than only narrate history. Humans crave an enemy, but Islam teaches that the real enemy is unseen: Shaytan only whispers, and the choice is ours. The West, having lost communism as its enemy, chose Muslims; even as Muslims became part of its schools, hospitals and politics, the establishment's view did not change. The same hatred and indifference that produced June 6 now lets tens of thousands die in Gaza while leaders say nothing. Should Muslims care how they are seen? Yes, as ambassadors of Allah's final word, and they change the narrative by being fully Muslim, not by compromising. He tells high school and university students that their voice carries weight without suspicion and has already moved public opinion. He recalls hearing the news of June 6 at the hospital, and shows how the Prophet guarded Islam's image, refusing to let Umar kill Ibn Ubayy. In the second khutbah he restates his five community objectives, education, mentorship, outreach, financial stability and advocacy, calls the youth to mature early like the young companions at Badr, and names indifference and the lack of a plan as what must change.

outline.heading: Opening
Two anniversaries: zoom out
outline.gist: Allah's promise is true; do not be deceived by this life, and treat Shaytan as the enemy he is (35:5-6). Gaza nears nine months and the June 6 attack on South Carriage Road nears its third anniversary; between the two Muslims must stop and reassess.

outline.heading: Narrating history without learning it
outline.gist: A people who cannot reflect will not make better choices. The fatal human flaw is narrating history as it happens while taking none of the lessons that would stop it recurring.

outline.heading: We crave an enemy; the real one is within
outline.gist: Humans need an enemy to channel hatred and blame. Islam says the enemy is unseen and weak: Shaytan only plants thoughts and confuses, and we make the final choice, so the enemy is mostly ourselves.

outline.heading: They cannot harm you, only make you harmful
outline.gist: The Quran ends with refuge from the whisperer among jinn and people (114:1-6): whisperers cannot harm you, but they can make you harmful.

outline.heading: From communism to Muslims
outline.gist: The West needs an enemy: for decades it was communism, as any 70s film shows, and then it fell on Muslims. Once Muslims immigrated and worked alongside people, it became harder to call them the enemy.

outline.heading: Part of the fabric, still the enemy
outline.gist: Muslims teach in Western schools, work in hospitals and run for office, yet the establishment's view is unchanged while 35,000 are dead, mostly women and children, many burned in their tents.

outline.heading: A refugee camp is not life
outline.gist: He has been to refugee camps: life there is limbo, and still they are hunted there. When Muslims ask why this is supported, there is no answer, because they are still seen as the enemy.

outline.heading: The indifference behind June 6 and Gaza
outline.gist: The political and social indifference that let the hatred behind June 6 build is what lets children be pulled from rubble and taken to hospitals without doctors, while the leaders Muslims vote for and pay taxes to say nothing.

outline.heading: The West still needs an enemy
outline.gist: His theory: the West has not matured enough to see it can run a country without an enemy, and keeps the narrative alive in media, news and films while Muslims have grown numb to it.

outline.heading: Should we even try to change the narrative?
outline.gist: Can Muslims change public opinion about Islam, and do they care to? The answers he hears are not united, and he argues that not caring is wrong.

outline.heading: Ambassadors of the final word
outline.gist: Muslims carry the Prophet's legacy and are commanded to represent Islam well and carry it to others; if they are failing, they must go back to the drawing board. Lifting injustice follows from that.

outline.heading: The weight of a young voice
outline.gist: University students have moved public opinion astonishingly in recent weeks. When an older man demands change people suspect an agenda; a young person's demand comes from a pure place, so throw that weight around.

outline.heading: Change it by being truly Muslim
outline.gist: Those who work in certain places know how Muslims are spoken of. The narrative changes by following the Quran and Sunnah exactly, not by compromising. June 6 changed the city and him forever.

outline.heading: Where he was when he heard
outline.gist: He was on call at University Hospital when a message asked if he had seen the news. He knew the family; the hatred was intolerable, his wife would not walk alone for months, and now imagine 35,000 or 37,000 dead.

outline.heading: Not a complex situation
outline.gist: Beyond the dead are the maimed and the trauma, yet the world treats it as complex and secondary. It is not complex. The obligation is to leave the next generation a better world and equip them to speak for themselves.

outline.heading: Safety and food: shelve your complaints
outline.gist: Outside any dictatorship, with safety and food, you have the only two blessings worth complaining about; take other complaints to Allah in sujud and teach your children to take stands for justice and truth.

outline.heading: No more far-fetched than Safa
outline.gist: Anything else is wasted breath. Changing how the world sees Islam is no more far-fetched than the Prophet calling his people from Safa with fewer than fifty followers, cursed by his own uncle; we are two billion and need only a few pure hearts.

outline.heading: 'People will never say Muhammad kills his companions'
outline.gist: Ibn Ubayy harmed the Prophet more than anyone. Returning from a long campaign he said something vile and refused to share supplies with hungry soldiers; Umar asked to strike his neck, and the Prophet refused and promised to be a good companion to him while he stayed.

outline.heading: One slip, and they could only call him mad
outline.gist: He cared how Islam would be seen; a single mistake would have ended the story. The disbelievers almost made him slip with their glares (68:51), and finding nothing, could only call him mad.

outline.heading: Interlude
Two fronts: politics and the narrative
outline.gist: The suffering overseas and the attack here share one root. The political front he leaves to others; the front of education, advocacy and the narrative about Muslims is one the community can steer.

outline.heading: Objective one: education
outline.gist: The first of the five community objectives he set two years ago: make sure the young know what they stand for and understand Islam as it is, so ignorance has no way in and they have an identity.

outline.heading: Objective two: mentorship
outline.gist: Mentorship is not a few programs but stepping up yourself so the person behind you watches and learns to step up too.

outline.heading: Objective three: outreach
outline.gist: The community must work harder to bring Islam to those who do not have it, a responsibility it will be asked about on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Objective four: financial stability
outline.gist: The community needs enough financial stability to fund the work that has to be done.

outline.heading: Objective five: advocacy
outline.gist: The most important objective: advocate for justice, rights and goodness, and be the voice of those who have none, like the poor who die quietly and are buried forgotten, so their lives were not in vain.

outline.heading: Grow up early, like Ali at ten
outline.gist: History sometimes asks the young to mature before their time, as Ali, Zubayr and others did at ten or twelve. Do not say you are too young; live differently and in thirty years a khatib can celebrate achievements instead of pain.

outline.heading: Why he keeps speaking of pain
outline.gist: These have been the hardest nine months of khutbahs in his life, and he is tempted to talk about uplifting things, but oppression must be named until it is removed or there is a plan to remove it.

outline.heading: What must change: indifference and no plan
outline.gist: Indifference and the lack of a plan or direction must change. Then the young will be proud and energized to be Muslim, come to the masjid and want to learn, without being begged to put down their phones.

outline.heading: Without a cause, people play games
outline.gist: People with no cause resort to meaningless play. A little awareness in old and young can make something almost magical happen; to him the magic of the seerah is its young people.

outline.heading: The boy at Badr
outline.gist: An eleven-year-old asked at Badr where Abu Jahl was, because he had harmed the Prophet and he had vowed not to come home without killing him; his sword was tied to his arm because it was too heavy.

outline.heading: Outro

B8APiSCsbjw.one_line: Al-Taghabun 5-9: forgetting why you act, the fate of those who defied, arrogance, accountability, iman as internalized knowledge, and the Day of mutual loss.
B8APiSCsbjw.summary: He places Al-Taghabun as a Medinan surah with a Meccan feel, set among surahs that organize the young Muslim community. Where those surahs give rules, this one gives none: it reminds the believer why he follows the rules at all. Using the image of a path that drifts by a fraction of a degree, he argues that any practice cut off from its purpose, pleasing Allah, slowly turns into something else, and he gives examples: political authority used to silence people, guardianship in marriage used for control, and parents forcing children to pray. Verse 5 summarizes the Quran's many stories of nations who lost both this life and the next, and he insists that a life of defiance is miserable now too, since fulfillment comes from purpose, not money or pleasure. Verse 6 shows the barrier was arrogance toward human messengers, and he explains how arrogance kills learning and growth. Verse 7 targets denial of accountability and answers it with four layers of emphasis. Verse 8 defines iman as internalizing knowledge until it guides behaviour, with the Quran as light that removes deception. Verse 9 names the Day of Gathering as the day all mutual fooling ends. He asks listeners to keep asking whether their actions please Allah and to review the major tests of their lives honestly.

outline.heading: Where Al-Taghabun sits: a Medinan surah with a Meccan feel
outline.gist: He recalls that the surah was revealed in Madinah yet reads like a Meccan one, sitting within a cluster of Medinan surahs that deal with organizing the Muslim community.

outline.heading: Fiqh is technical; this surah is not
outline.gist: Jurisprudence only states what is allowed and required; this surah steps back from technicalities to speak of meaning.

outline.heading: The compass: staying tied to the destination
outline.gist: A path that drifts by half a degree ends up galaxies away; only a constant connection to the end point keeps you straight, wherever you start from.

outline.heading: Madinah built on people and principles, and the risk of forgetting why
outline.gist: The Prophet built a state in the desert by investing in people for thirteen years before adding rules; once things prosper, people maintain institutions just because they are theirs.

outline.heading: Rulings misused when their purpose is forgotten
outline.gist: Obedience to the ruler becomes a tool of dictatorship and the guardian in marriage becomes a means of control when people forget why Allah placed these rulings.

outline.heading: Taghabun: mutual fooling, and a surah with no rulings
outline.gist: The surah's name means fooling and being fooled; unlike its neighbours it holds no legal rulings, only Allah's grace and advice.

outline.heading: The test question: will this please Allah?
outline.gist: Before acting ask whether it pleases Allah; forcing young people or one's children into worship fails that test.

outline.heading: Nothing is worth preserving at all costs except Islam itself
outline.gist: Even a beloved centre matters only while it serves Allah; step back from work and family and ask whether you are achieving the real goal, even if that means admitting you were wrong.

outline.heading: Recap: Allah presents His majesty
outline.gist: The first four verses introduce who you are serving through His main attributes.

outline.heading: The news of those who defied: a verse that summarizes much of the Quran
outline.gist: Verse 5 condenses the repeated stories of earlier nations who tasted the consequences of their choices in this life and face punishment in the next.

outline.heading: Lose both or win both: the illusion of fun now
outline.gist: The Quran does not offer good now and bad later; defiance is miserable in this life too, and its temporary highs only deepen the inner emptiness.

outline.heading: Fulfillment comes from purpose, not money
outline.gist: Beyond a modest income money does not raise long-term happiness; fulfillment comes from living for something beyond yourself, and fully from living for Allah.

outline.heading: Messengers came with bayyinat: clarifications
outline.gist: Revelation is described as clarifications of what people can partly reach on their own, and clarity leaves no room to be fooled.

outline.heading: "Shall humans guide us?": arrogance blocks learning
outline.gist: Their objection was to the human messenger; arrogance means endless comparison, refusing to learn from others and only hearing what one wants to hear.

outline.heading: They turned away, and Allah is free of need, Praiseworthy
outline.gist: Istaghna means not needing someone, not wealth; Allah needs no one and is praiseworthy whether or not He is praised, so the clarifications were sent for our sake.

outline.heading: The same arrogance ruins Muslims' practice
outline.gist: A little pride inside skews any work done for Allah over time; always ask whom you are serving.

outline.heading: Interlude
Their claim: the real denial is accountability, not resurrection
outline.gist: Resurrection is easy to accept if Allah created the first time; people reject being held accountable, often by blaming their circumstances.

outline.heading: The questions you will be asked, and the big tests of your life
outline.gist: Life holds a handful of major highs and lows that will be questioned in detail; review how you have done on them.

outline.heading: "Bala wa rabbi": four layers of emphasis
outline.gist: He breaks down the negation, the oath, the lam and the heavy nun of emphasis: you will be raised and informed of what you did, and that is easy for Allah.

outline.heading: Iman as internalized understanding
outline.gist: Iman means knowledge that sinks from the surface of awareness into the depths where it guides behaviour, as with facts we know about smoking or fast food but ignore.

outline.heading: The Quran as light that ends deception
outline.gist: Light lets you see things as they are, so temptations and Shaytan's tricks cannot fool you.

outline.heading: Khabir: Allah knows why you act
outline.gist: Beyond seeing your deeds, He knows your reasons; check whether you pray and fast because others do or because you will be asked.

outline.heading: Interlude
The grammar of conditional verbs and the logic of Arabic
outline.gist: He explains why the verbs after the condition take sukun, a verb held captive by the condition, as an example of how logical and majestic Arabic is.

outline.heading: The Day of Gathering: the day all fooling ends
outline.gist: Taghabun is mutual fooling going back and forth; on that Day every web of self-deception and lies is undone and only the truth remains.

28:28.ar: قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَكَۖ أَيَّمَا ٱلۡأَجَلَيۡنِ قَضَيۡتُ فَلَا عُدۡوَٰنَ عَلَيَّۖ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلࣱ‏
28:28.en: He said: That (is settled) between thee and me. Whichever of the two terms I fulfil, there will be no injustice to me, and Allah is Surety over what we say

28:29.ar: ۞فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلۡأَجَلَ وَسَارَ بِأَهۡلِهِۦٓ ءَانَسَ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ نَارࣰ اۖ قَالَ لِأَهۡلِهِ ٱمۡكُثُوٓاْ إِنِّيٓ ءَانَسۡتُ نَارࣰ ا لَّعَلِّيٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنۡهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوۡ جَذۡوَةࣲ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَصۡطَلُونَ
28:29.en: Then, when Moses had fulfilled the term, and was travelling with his housefolk, he saw in the distance a fire and said unto his housefolk: Bide ye (here). Lo! I see in the distance a fire; peradventure I shall bring you tidings thence, or a brand from the fire that ye may warm yourselves

28:30.ar: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِيَ مِن شَٰطِيِٕ ٱلۡوَادِ ٱلۡأَيۡمَنِ فِي ٱلۡبُقۡعَةِ ٱلۡمُبَٰرَكَةِ مِنَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ أَن يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّيٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
28:30.en: And when he reached it, he was called from the right side of the valley in the blessed field, from the tree: O Moses! Lo! I, even I, am Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

28:31.ar: وَأَنۡ أَلۡقِ عَصَاكَۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهۡتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنࣱّ وَلَّىٰ مُدۡبِرࣰ ا وَلَمۡ يُعَقِّبۡۚ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَقۡبِلۡ وَلَا تَخَفۡۖ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓمِنِينَ
28:31.en: Throw down thy staff. And when he saw it writhing as it had been a demon, he turned to flee headlong, (and it was said unto him): O Moses! Draw nigh and fear not. Lo! thou art of those who are secure

28:27.ar: قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أُنكِحَكَ إِحۡدَى ٱبۡنَتَيَّ هَٰتَيۡنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأۡجُرَنِي ثَمَٰنِيَ حِجَجࣲۖ فَإِنۡ أَتۡمَمۡتَ عَشۡرࣰ ا فَمِنۡ عِندِكَۖ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أَشُقَّ عَلَيۡكَۚ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
28:27.en: He said: Lo! I fain would marry thee to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that thou hirest thyself to me for (the term of) eight pilgrimages. Then if thou completest ten it will be of thine own accord, for I would not make it hard for thee. Allah willing, thou wilt find me of the righteous

20:25.en: (Moses) said: My Lord! relieve my mind

20:26.en: And ease my task for me

20:27.en: And loose a knot from my tongue

20:28.en: That they may understand my saying

28:34.ar: وَأَخِي هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفۡصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانࣰ ا فَأَرۡسِلۡهُ مَعِيَ رِدۡءࣰ ا يُصَدِّقُنِيٓۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
28:34.en: My brother Aaron is more eloquent than me in speech. Therefor send him with me as a helper to confirm me. Lo! I fear that they will give the lie to me

43:52.ar: أَمۡ أَنَا۠ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينࣱ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ
43:52.en: I am surely better than this fellow, who is despicable and can hardly make (his meaning) plain

8:7.ar: وَإِذۡ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ إِحۡدَى ٱلطَّآئِفَتَيۡنِ أَنَّهَا لَكُمۡ وَتَوَدُّونَ أَنَّ غَيۡرَ ذَاتِ ٱلشَّوۡكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمۡ وَيُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُحِقَّ ٱلۡحَقَّ بِكَلِمَٰتِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعَ دَابِرَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
8:7.en: And when Allah promised you one of the two bands (of the enemy) that it should be yours, and ye longed that other than the armed one might be yours. And Allah willed that He should cause the Truth to triumph by His words, and cut the root of the disbelievers

8:8.ar: لِيُحِقَّ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَيُبۡطِلَ ٱلۡبَٰطِلَ وَلَوۡ كَرِهَ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ
8:8.en: That He might cause the Truth to triumph and bring vanity to naught, however much the guilty might oppose

27:8.ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا نُودِيَ أَنۢ بُورِكَ مَن فِي ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنۡ حَوۡلَهَا وَسُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
27:8.en: But when he reached it, he was called, saying: Blessed is Whosoever is in the fire and Whosoever is round about it! And Glorified be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

27:9.ar: يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
27:9.en: O Moses! Lo! it is I, Allah, the Mighty, the Wise

20:11.en: And when he reached it, he was called by name: O Moses

20:12.ar: إِنِّيٓ أَنَا۠ رَبُّكَ فَٱخۡلَعۡ نَعۡلَيۡكَ إِنَّكَ بِٱلۡوَادِ ٱلۡمُقَدَّسِ طُوࣰ ى
20:12.en: Lo! I, even I, am thy Lord, So take off thy shoes, for lo! thou art in the holy valley of Tuwa

20:13.en: And I have chosen thee, so hearken unto that which is inspired

20:14.ar: إِنَّنِيٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعۡبُدۡنِي وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكۡرِيٓ
20:14.en: Lo! I, even I, am Allah, There is no Allah save Me. So serve Me and establish worship for My remembrance

23:20.ar: وَشَجَرَةࣰ تَخۡرُجُ مِن طُورِ سَيۡنَآءَ تَنۢبُتُ بِٱلدُّهۡنِ وَصِبۡغࣲ لِّلۡأٓكِلِينَ
23:20.en: And a tree that springeth forth from Mount Sinai that groweth oil and relish for the eaters

20:17.en: And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses

20:18.ar: قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّؤُاْ عَلَيۡهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِي وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخۡرَىٰ
20:18.en: He said: This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I bear down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses

27:10.ar: وَأَلۡقِ عَصَاكَۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهۡتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنࣱّ وَلَّىٰ مُدۡبِرࣰ ا وَلَمۡ يُعَقِّبۡۚ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفۡ إِنِّي لَا يَخَافُ لَدَيَّ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلُونَ
27:10.en: And throw down thy staff! But when he saw it writhing as it were a demon, he turned to flee headlong; (but it was said unto him): O Moses! Fear not! the emissaries fear not in My presence

27:11.ar: إِلَّا مَن ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسۡنَۢا بَعۡدَ سُوٓءࣲ فَإِنِّي غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
27:11.en: Save him who hath done wrong and afterward hath changed evil for good. And lo! I am Forgiving, Merciful

6XcejCIT068.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat al-Qasas, the Fire on the Mount (28:28-31)
6XcejCIT068.one_line: From Madyan to the Mount: seeing a man's true metal, the hidden sacred spot, the uncreated speech of Allah, and Imam Ahmad's stand.
6XcejCIT068.summary: He returns to the marriage offer: the old man of Madyan looked past a hungry, barefoot stranger who could not speak well and saw his true metal, a man who served without asking anything. Judged by appearances he would have married his daughter to a wealthy suitor; instead he offered kinship, refused to burden him, and gained a man who would protect her. Musa agreed while keeping his mission to return to his enslaved people. Reciting the next verses he discusses recitation habits across regions, the seven modes, and why advanced readings take years. On the location of the Mount and the blessed spot, he argues Allah hid it wisely, perhaps to prevent bloodshed over it, and he digresses into Zionist ambitions on Sinai and the long history of Jews living safely among Muslims. Before explaining 'I am Allah, Lord of the worlds', he explains the creed: Allah's speech is eternal while the sounds and letters conveying it are created. The trial over the Quran's createdness was really about the scholar's freedom from political dictation, and Imam Ahmad's firmness saved the religion; today's religious institution has lost respect for lacking that independence. Musa came for a firebrand and received prophethood, fled from his staff, and was told to come forward without fear, an honour for his intention to rescue his people.

outline.heading: Musa's story and its likeness to the Prophet's
outline.gist: No prophet's story is told at such length as Musa's, and no prophet resembles the Prophet more.

outline.heading: Recap: I know only what Allah shows me of you
outline.gist: The surah is named for stories because only Allah knows our inner reality; each scene so far would mislead an onlooker.

outline.heading: The old man's wisdom and Musa's halting speech
outline.gist: Whether the old man was a prophet is uncertain; his wisdom was striking, as Musa was no speaker and knew it.

outline.heading: Harun as spokesman, Pharaoh's taunt, Musa at the Throne
outline.gist: Musa asked for Harun because his chest tightened before crowds; Pharaoh mocked him, yet on the Day he is seen holding the Throne.

outline.heading: Looking for the metal, not the surface
outline.gist: The old man asked his daughters questions and found a man who helped and asked for nothing.

outline.heading: The noble serves without wanting anything
outline.gist: A base man helps women hoping for something in return; Musa, so hungry he had eaten leaves, asked not even for a wage.

outline.heading: Had he judged by appearance
outline.gist: He would have married her to a rich man with a car and an apartment; instead he had the courage to marry her to a stranger and not burden him.

outline.heading: Offering kinship, not a job, and not marrying her cheaply
outline.gist: He gained the most precious thing, a man who would care for and bear with his daughter.

outline.heading: Musa's reply: no grievance between us
outline.gist: Whichever term he fulfils, no resentment; he had a mission to return and free his people.

outline.heading: Marriage and honest work in Madyan
outline.gist: Allah joined the good man with the good woman; he worked for his father-in-law until the term was done.

outline.heading: Reciting tastalun
outline.gist: The light ta and emphatic sad sit side by side; the tongue wants to make both heavy or both light.

outline.heading: Different tongues, different challenges
outline.gist: Students in Syria had to learn lightness, those here the opposite; the seven modes were a mercy for differing tongues.

outline.heading: Recitation variants in practice
outline.gist: He shortens the separated elongation in prayer; varying readings in prayer accustoms people to them, while full study of the readings takes years.

outline.heading: Which term did he fulfil?
outline.gist: A report says the longer, but the verse leaves it open since they agreed there would be no grievance.

outline.heading: Travelling with his family
outline.gist: Ahl in the Quran means wife and children; consulting one's wife before travel is a good habit.

outline.heading: Where is the Mount?
outline.gist: Its exact location in Sinai is uncertain despite historians' claims.

outline.heading: Ambitions on Sinai and the land of Ibrahim
outline.gist: The occupying state will not stop at Gaza; replacing one oppressor with another achieves nothing, only truth removes falsehood.

outline.heading: Jews lived safely among Muslims
outline.gist: Jewish quarters existed for centuries in Damascus, Baghdad and elsewhere, and their own historians record no massacres by Muslims; our grasp of the region's history is shallow.

outline.heading: I perceived a fire: news or a firebrand
outline.gist: Lost on the road with no map, he left his family to seek directions or warmth.

outline.heading: I am Allah, Lord of the worlds
outline.gist: Compared with the parallel accounts in an-Naml and Ta-Ha, this one sums it all in a few words; 'alamin means everything other than Allah.

outline.heading: The right side of the valley, the blessed spot
outline.gist: Shati' means any bank, not only a seashore; the right side may be reckoned facing Al-Aqsa, the qiblah then.

outline.heading: Why Allah hid the place
outline.gist: If known, people might kill each other over it; even the Jews do not know the exact mountain, and the olive tree of Sinai is a clue.

outline.heading: Creed must be understood
outline.gist: All schools revere and declare Allah's oneness and reject anthropomorphism, yet differ in their explanations.

outline.heading: When Muslims fought over their schools
outline.gist: Shafi'is and Malikis would not pray behind each other and at-Tabari was killed; adopting a school brought calm.

outline.heading: Allah's speech is an eternal attribute
outline.gist: Among His attributes of meaning are hearing, sight, will, power and speech; His speech is eternal, not originated.

outline.heading: What did Musa hear?
outline.gist: The Quran is uncreated, but written letters and recited sounds are created; Musa heard created sound carrying eternal meaning.

outline.heading: A minor creed question made a test
outline.gist: The Prophet and companions did not discuss it, so it need not ruin anyone's faith, yet the caliph al-Ma'mun imposed one view.

outline.heading: Imam Ahmad's stand: freedom of the scholar
outline.gist: He refused to let politics dictate a scholar's view; as a doctor in his clinic, the scholar must speak by what he sees, and his firmness saved the religion.

outline.heading: Today's religious institution has lost respect
outline.gist: Persecution and enforced uniformity ruined it; an unfit or muzzled speaker on the minbar corrupts the religion.

outline.heading: One Jumuah per city
outline.gist: Scholars disliked several Friday congregations in one town; ash-Shafi'i said where two exist the people should also pray dhuhr.

outline.heading: He came for fire and received prophethood
outline.gist: Better than news or a firebrand, he heard Allah's speech.

outline.heading: Reciting 'as if it were a jann'
outline.gist: Six counts for the elongation, then the doubled nun and the partial merging, ten counts in all.

outline.heading: The staff moves like a jann and he flees
outline.gist: Jann means something moving uncontrollably; Musa turned and fled, as the Prophet came home trembling after the first revelation.

outline.heading: Come forward and do not fear
outline.gist: Messengers need not fear before Allah; Musa was spoken to because he intended to return and rescue his people.

themes.label: Not judging others by their story
themes.note: The old man of Madyan looked past Musa's appearance to his true metal, the one correct judgement in the story.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Choose a son-in-law for character, offer kinship, do not burden him; this is not marrying a daughter cheaply.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
